items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-03-22
items.q: He asked me, would I play their ball? He said, they were dissatisfied with the Neville brothers.

ctx.x: Did you feel you were appreciated more by whites?

I'll tell you what. And you just ask. Start with the Neville brothers, Irma Thomas, Gene Knight, Oliver. And just ask them. They're going to tell you the same thing I'm saying. Hey, man, look. If there was a way. Well, I could. You know. Now, playing these social clubs is a different thing because you get set into playing a certain way. Okay. You know that people are going to come in there and sit down. You know the other people are going to sit down until they get half juice. And then they'll let loose. And we…
Because you don't work, you know, to black audiences, I'm saying, you were working to whites, did blacks ever tell you, you know, why don't you play for your own kind?
